treatment.logline: A returned phone opens a tentative connection beside a modest Colombo food business, until a family call changes the space between two new acquaintances.

arc.beat: A practical kindness becomes personal curiosity.
His ambition earns her admiration; the phone interrupts.
An unseen demand erases her ease.
Their farewell leaves the connection unresolved.

treatment.approach: Grounded romantic social drama, not heightened suspense: let shared frames build equality, then isolate Anudi during the call. Rain-shaped daylight and restrained acting carry the interruption without a weather or lighting change. All material is essential continuous-action coverage; the bin runs above the nominal target because complete dialogue, visible actions and minimal edit handles must coexist.

treatment.geography: Anudi stands frame left facing right; Kasun stands frame right facing left. The food three-wheeler sits behind Kasun to the right. advice: Preserve the short interested looks without manufacturing attraction through extra gestures.
The caller is audio only; Kasun notices her face, not the contents of the remote audio.
Use a readable Father caller ID before the remote voice begins.
Keep physical rain and daylight continuous; let performance create the tonal turn.

editor_notes: The 12 must takes total 62 seconds, including internal handles, against a 45-second intended scene and 67.5-second cap. Trim handles and use natural overlap across matched positions to build the intended cut; do not shorten any line.

4A shared frames carry the return, exchange and return from the call; 4B and 4C hold individual speakers, 4D makes the incoming caller ID legible with Anudi's reaction, 4E holds the call and its effect, and 4F preserves both departure paths.

Match the phone from Kasun's right hand into Anudi's right hand, then at her right ear and back down; keep the open umbrella in her left hand and the handbag on her left forearm. The opening offer comes from the preceding scene; the explicit handover resolves the conflicting start-state shorthand.

Show the readable Father caller ID before L11. The ring and remote audio can be added in post; L11 remains private to Anudi and the audience, and Kasun reacts only to her visible expression. Composite the ID if the generated text is unreliable.

C03 and C09 have tight handles because both contain a complete timed action and line; preserve the full performances. The speech-clock lead and tail supplement the short explicit handles on C02, C04 and C05.
Use a phone-masked handover or invisible edit rather than demanding visible body contact or fast finger work. Avoid mirrors, sharp crowds and invented business activities.

The locked clean frames can support a restrained digital punch-in if the editor needs it; speed ramp, freeze frame and split screen are post-only and are not required by this scene. No generated slow motion is applied to dialogue.

Wardrobe colours and hand assignments are continuity choices, not script facts; match them to the preceding scene before generation. Keep rain, overcast light, character appearances and the modest three-wheeler continuous.

editor_notes: The 12 must takes total 62 seconds, including internal handles, against a 45-second intended scene and 67.5-second cap. Trim handles and use natural overlap across matched positions to build the intended cut; do not shorten any line.

4A shared frames carry the return, exchange and return from the call; 4B and 4C hold individual speakers, 4D makes the incoming caller ID legible with Anudi's reaction, 4E holds the call and its effect, and 4F preserves both departure paths.

Match the phone from Kasun's right hand into Anudi's right hand, then at her right ear and back down; keep the open umbrella in her left hand and the handbag on her left forearm. The opening offer comes from the preceding scene; the explicit handover resolves the conflicting start-state shorthand.

Show the readable Father caller ID before L11. The ring and remote audio can be added in post; L11 remains private to Anudi and the audience, and Kasun reacts only to her visible expression. Composite the ID if the generated text is unreliable.

C03 and C09 have tight handles because both contain a complete timed action and line; preserve the full performances. The speech-clock lead and tail supplement the short explicit handles on C02, C04 and C05.
Use a phone-masked handover or invisible edit rather than demanding visible body contact or fast finger work. Avoid mirrors, sharp crowds and invented business activities.

The locked clean frames can support a restrained digital punch-in if the editor needs it; speed ramp, freeze frame and split screen are post-only and are not required by this scene. No generated slow motion is applied to dialogue.

Wardrobe colours and hand assignments are continuity choices, not script facts; match them to the preceding scene before generation. Keep rain, overcast light, character appearances and the modest three-wheeler continuous.
